unresolved_added: The multilevel hierarchy, variance inflation, pooling strength, and local likelihoods are not fully specified.
Goodness is described as GDP plus salary while displayed equations use tuition and enrollment; the outcome bridge is incomplete.
RoI alternates among change in Goodness, a Goodness/resource slope, and reported table values without a unit ledger.
The jobs-added formula appears to multiply degree share twice after Students already includes it.
An uncertain labor-market proxy becomes a hard exclusion when estimated jobs added are negative.
Field unemployment comes from different years and is assumed stable across fields and five future years.
The displayed GDP regression omits an explicit fitted slope coefficient.
Log of a GDP change is domain-sensitive and conflicts with language closer to a change in log GDP.
The long historical GDP-unemployment series has no released stationarity, autocorrelation, break, or holdout checks.
A historical association is used as the effect of university-induced jobs without causal identification.
Q-Q, residual, and actual-versus-predicted plots challenge Normality, constant variance, and model form.
Close enough and final satisfaction claims provide no severity threshold for diagnostic violations.
Simply missing data are assigned MCAR without a diagnostic proving independence.
The MAR regression omits covariates, estimates, convergence, and imputation diagnostics.
Variance-versus-precision notation is ambiguous and must be reconciled with BUGS parameterization.
The paper claims full uncertainty accountability but allocations lack posterior decision distributions.
Yearly results vary national forecasts while school characteristics remain effectively cross-sectional.
Public-school and community-college funding multipliers are ad hoc and partly justified by resulting outputs.
The greedy routine has no proof of global optimality for the capped nonlinear multiyear decision.
Algorithm 1 appears to subtract enrollment rather than a clearly defined dollar increment.
The concentration cap is selected without elicitation, sensitivity, or an explicit institution-risk model.
Recognizable universities are used as legitimacy evidence; this is face validity, not outcome validation.
Many reported RoI values are nearly identical despite different grants, without a precision or saturation explanation.
No executable code, cleaned snapshot, chain diagnostics, seed, optimizer trace, or allocation certificate is released.
The donor letter and final conclusion express confidence more strongly than residual and data limitations support.
